lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Reteach and varied practice: random sampling

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: These two examples show the same idea in two different formats.

items.prompt: In a random sample of 20 students, 8 preferred pizza. Based on this sample, about how many of the 200 students in the school would you expect to prefer pizza?

steps: Find the sample proportion: 8 out of 20 preferred pizza.
Scale up to the population: the school is 200 ÷ 20 = 10 times the sample size.

items.prompt: Five random samples of the same population produced these mean scores: 72, 75, 68, 74, 71. What is the range of these sample estimates?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A population has 443 students at Lincoln Middle School. Student A takes a random sample of 19. Student B takes a random sample of 60. Both use proper random selection. Whose sample is more likely to give an estimate closer to the true population value?
choices: Both are equally likely to be accurate, because both are random.
Student A's sample of 19, because smaller samples are easier to analyze.
Student B's sample of 60, because larger random samples tend to produce more consistent, accurate estimates.
Neither sample is reliable unless it includes the entire population.

items.prompt: A student surveys 10 students at Lincoln Middle School using a simple random sample and records the results. Is it valid to generalize this result to all 150 students at Lincoln Middle School?
choices: Yes, because the sample size is large enough regardless of how it was chosen.
No, because the sample was not randomly selected, so it may not represent the population.
No, because samples can never be generalized to a population.
Yes, because the sample was selected randomly, so it is likely representative of the population.

items.prompt: A sample of 6 values is: 9, 8, 25, 10, 13, 8. What is the range of this data set?
A data set has 5 values: 20, 20, 20, 17, 15. What is the new mean if an outlier of 48 is added to the data set, making 6 values in all?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A data set is: 20, 17, 20, 23, with a mean of 20. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of this data set?
Two data sets have means of 60 and 66. Their mean absolute deviation (MAD) is 6. Express the difference between the means as a multiple of the MAD.
choices: 3 times the MAD
0 times the MAD
6 times the MAD
1 times the MAD

items.prompt: Sample A: 26, 34, 38, 34, 8. Sample B: 43, 29, 31, 39, 53. Based on the means, which sample tends to have greater values?
choices: Sample A, with a mean of 28 compared to 39.
Sample B, with a mean of 39 compared to 28.
Sample B, with a mean of 28 compared to 39.
Both samples have the same mean.

items.prompt: Sample A: 26, 31, 31, 18, 41, 38. Sample B: 29, 27, 27, 26, 27, 27. Based on the range of each sample, which sample is more consistent (less variable)?
choices: Sample A, with a range of 23 compared to 3.
Sample B, with a range of 23 compared to 3.
Both samples have the same range.
Sample B, with a range of 3 compared to 23.

items.prompt: A researcher wants to know about all 1932 shoppers at a grocery store. She randomly selects 352 of them to survey. What is the sample in this situation?
choices: Only the first 352 shoppers at a grocery store on a list
All 1932 shoppers at a grocery store
The 352 randomly selected shoppers at a grocery store
The researcher's own estimate
